newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis demand state inquiry of scandal.
newsitem.headline: Israelis demand state inquiry of scandal.

text.p: Several thousand Israelis rallied opposite Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office in Jerusalem on Saturday demanding a state commission be set up to investigate a government influence-peddling scandal.
Demonstrators using Netanyahu's nickname chanted: "Bibi resign, Israel is more important".
Organisers estimated the crowd at 10,000 but Israel's Channel Two television put the number at about 2,000.

Retired high court judge Haim Cohen, at a meeting earlier in the day with the citizens group pushing for the state inquiry, said Netanyahu should have resigned after prosecutors last month decided not to charge him for lack of evidence despite "real suspicions" over his role in the affair.

"Any person, any statesman who really respects himself and knows his obligation and has some compass defined for himself would not have to be pushed to resign, the public wouldn't have to be dragged into it," Cohen said in remarks broadcast by Channel Two.
Netanyahu spokesman Shai Bazak said the drive for a state commission of inquiry was politically motivated and had nothing to do with good government.
"The public understands the clear political motives of the protest and its organisers from the left against the Israeli government," he said in a statement to the media.
A Channel One television report spurred a police inquiry into the short-lived appointment of Likud activist and lawyer Roni Bar-On as attorney general in January.

It alleged Shas religious party legislator Aryeh Deri, already on trial for corruption, coerced Netanyahu into appointing Bar-On, who would offer him a plea bargain. Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid a public outcry that he was a legal lightweight unqualified for the job.
Police, after a three-month investigation recommended Netanyahu, his justice minister and others be charged.
Prosecutors decided to charge only Deri. They said Netanyahu's director-general, Avigdor Lieberman, should face further questioning.
Netanyahu said the prosecutors' decision vindicated him though he admitted mistakes and vowed to correct them.
In addition to the call for a state inquiry, opposition lawmakers have appealed to the High Court to charge Netanyahu. The court is to hold its first hearing later this month.
